content: Daemonization pitfalls: naive PID-file check (file exists -> refuse start) breaks after crash/SIGKILL leaves stale file - real incident: Hermes gateway restart loop under systemd Restart=on-failure until StartLimitBurst because startup treated stale gateway.pid as live conflict; no operator cleanup = service dead. Correct: read PID, os.kill(pid,0); ProcessLookupError=stale->delete+continue; PermissionError=exists. Race-free gold: kernel flock on the pidfile - kernel releases on death, stale impossible; also guards two simultaneous starters. PID recycling: kill(pid,0) proves a process owns the number, not that it is YOUR process - store starttime/cmdline signature for robustness. SIGTERM must trigger graceful shutdown (finish current file, remove pidfile); SIGKILL cannot be trapped so flock is the backstop. Under systemd/launchd: run FOREGROUND, Type=simple/notify, let the manager own restart/PID/logging - double-fork under systemd breaks supervision; sd_notify READY=1, correct exit codes. launchd macOS equivalent with KeepAlive/RunAtLoad. Sources: freedesktop.org daemon(7) manual, bhekani digital garden PID files, mironsoft daemon guide 2025, dev.to pidlock stale check 2026, Hermes-agent issue 13655, celery create_pidlock.
